name: Aluminium
occurrence: The most abundant metal in Earth's crust, mainly extracted from bauxite ore.
notableCharacteristics: Forms a microscopically thin, tough oxide layer instantly on exposure to air, which is exactly what protects it from further corrosion without needing paint.
whyHere: Three valence electrons let it form a stable +3 ion, and the resulting Al₂O₃ layer is so tightly bound to the metal surface that it self-seals against further oxygen exposure — the real secret behind aluminium's 'rust-proof' reputation.
didYouKnow: Aluminium was once more precious than gold — Napoleon III reportedly reserved aluminium cutlery for his most honoured guests before the Hall-Héroult process made it cheap to produce.
genZNote: Used to be fancier than gold, now it's your soda can. Glow-down or glow-up depends how you look at it.
